title: BSP warns public against fake bank closure claims
summary: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) has warned the public about a fake social media video claiming that banks in the country would close on Friday, November 20, adding that it may take action…
byline: JON VIKTOR D. CABUENAS, GMA News

blocks.text: Original image with 'fake' stamp provided by the BSP. GMA News Online obscured the face of the unidentified individual in this image.

The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) has warned the public about a fake social media video claiming that banks in the country would close on Friday, November 20, adding that it may take action against peddlers of fake news.
In an advisory, the BSP said the post was originally shared on Facebook, which has already taken down the video.
However, BSP warned that the video may still be circulating, reposted, or copied.
"The BSP is prepared to take action against any persons or organizations involved in creating or spreading the material or any similar fake news," the advisory issued on Wednesday read.
The central bank has also called on the public to report misleading posts or claims via its email bspmail@bsp.gov.ph. — VDV, GMA News
